title: Exec update — Route-level experiments (A/B testing) — March 2025
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Route-level experiments (A/B testing) — Weekly exec update (March 2025)
Owner: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts)
Eng leads: Dylan Brooks (Console), Ethan Park (Control plane), Logan Wright (Telemetry), Sean Gallagher (SRE)

Slide 2 — TL;DR (what changed since last week)
• We are functionally “end-to-end” in beta shape: experiment config → deterministic assignment at routing → attribution in telemetry → Console results view (basic deltas + guardrail status).
• Beta readiness is gated on two issues: (1) guardrail signal quality (false positives/negatives) and (2) config propagation lag / results staleness perception.
• We need 2–3 focused SRE days to complete alert tuning + runbooks + auto-stop kill switch review, and ~1 design sprint of bandwidth to resolve results-view clarity + guardrail UX copy.

Slide 3 — Goal + why now
Goal: ship safe route-level A/B/n experiments with first-class measurement hooks (latency/cost/errors + optional eval scores) directly in Console Rollouts.
Why now:
• Customers are already doing “shadow A/B” via multiple routes and external dashboards; they want a single workflow with deterministic bucketing and guardrails.
• This feature is a cornerstone for “production economics” positioning (measured cost/latency tradeoffs across model variants).

Slide 4 — Current phase status (vs plan)
Plan recap:
• Phase 1 (Feb): Control plane APIs + router integration behind feature flag; basic metrics attribution.
• Phase 2 (Mar): Console workflow + dashboards; eval-score hook integration; beta with design partners.
• Phase 3 (Apr): Hardening (SRE runbooks/alerts), RBAC/audit logging completeness; GA rollout.

Status (week of Mar 24):
• Control plane: DONE for beta (create/update/start/stop; validation; versioning).
• Data plane routing: DONE for beta (deterministic bucketing; stickiness precedence; apply experiment selection before fallback).
• Telemetry: DONE for beta (experiment_id + variant_id in request context and OTel spans; rollup tables powering Console).
• Console: MVP DONE (create wizard + list + detail + results dashboard; guardrail banners; audit history view in progress).
• Evals hook: PARTIAL (variant tagging in eval output available; wiring to Console quality metric behind flag).
• SRE hardening: IN PROGRESS (propagation lag + attribution drop alerts drafted; runbooks in review).

Slide 5 — Customer beta program snapshot
Design partners / early beta:
• Acme AI (CS deep dive Feb 6): needs model-variant A/B with strict p99 latency guardrails.
• Northbridge (POC scoping Feb 18): focused on cost attribution (cost/token) and auditability.
• Helio Financial (security review Mar 19): focused on audit logging, retention, export, and RBAC.

Beta success criteria (draft):
• Deterministic assignment stability > 99.9% (no drift for stable sticky key).
• Attribution drop rate < 0.5% on non-streaming and < 1.0% on streaming/retry paths.
• Results latency (time-to-fresh metrics) within agreed window for Console display; no “stale” confusion.
• Guardrails detect obvious regressions without excessive false positives; clear operator workflow for stop/rollback.

Slide 6 — What’s shipped in product terms (beta scope)
Workflow:
• Create experiment on a route (A/B/n), define variants (e.g., model version / quant profile), set traffic splits.
• Deterministic assignment using stickiness keys with safe defaults; supports missing IDs with warnings.
• Observe: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, throughput; cost metrics (tokens + cost/token) per variant.
• Guardrails: configurable thresholds, degradation banners, notifications; soft-stop default. Optional hard-stop for severe regressions behind a kill switch.
• Audit log: create/update/start/stop events; exports in progress for enterprise asks.

Slide 7 — Top metric + experience improvements this week
• Added propagation lag metric surfaced to dashboards (config staleness / cache propagation).
• Reduced metrics cardinality risk by limiting high-cardinality dimensions in always-on metrics; expanded detail via sampled traces.
• Fixed missing attribution on streaming retries (previously lost experiment fields across retry path).
• Console results query performance improvements (rolling up hot queries; caching for “top routes”).

Slide 8 — Remaining work to enter broader beta (next 1–2 weeks)
Beta gate checklist (practical):
1) Guardrails
• Default thresholds finalized; UI copy explains what is enforced vs observed.
• Soft-stop semantics: consistent state machine and operator expectations.
• Auto-stop: kill switch + SRE-reviewed alerting/false-positive mitigation.

2) Data quality & freshness
• Attribution drop rate alert tuned to avoid noise.
• Propagation lag alert thresholds validated in staging + one game day scenario.
• Clear “data freshness” indicator in Console results view.

3) Enterprise basics
• RBAC for start/stop/update consistent with existing Rollouts permissions.
• Audit event fields meet enterprise requirements (actor, diff summary, request ID, timestamps, retention note).

Slide 9 — Risks / issues (top 3)
1) Guardrail accuracy and trust
• Risk: false positives trigger unnecessary stops; false negatives allow regressions into prod.
• Root causes observed: low traffic variance at small splits; streaming latency distributions; cost metrics lag.
• Mitigation:
  – Make soft-stop the default; hard-stop only for severe, sustained p99 regression and behind a kill switch.
  – Use minimum sample / time window for evaluation (avoid reacting to noisy early minutes).
  – Display confidence cues (insufficient data) rather than “green check”.

2) Config propagation lag / perceived staleness
• Risk: Console shows stale results or wrong variant allocations; operators lose confidence.
• Root causes: cache refresh intervals, cross-region propagation delays, plus aggregation job schedule.
• Mitigation:
  – Ship propagation lag metric + alert; show config version and “last applied” time in Console.
  – Tighten staleness bounds; define behavior when config unavailable (safe fallback).
  – Game day: simulate lag and validate runbook + rollback.

3) Metrics cardinality & cost blowups
• Risk: adding experiment dimensions to all metrics increases cost and threatens observability budgets.
• Mitigation:
  – Restrict always-on tags to {route_id_normalized, experiment_id, variant_id} with careful limits; shift detail to sampled traces.
  – Enforce max variants; block overlapping experiments on same route (or require explicit priority) to bound combinations.

Slide 10 — Key decisions needed from leadership
Decision A: What do we promise for GA guardrails?
• Option 1 (recommended): GA includes soft-stop + notifications + manual stop/rollback; hard-stop remains optional behind kill switch and “advanced” setting.
• Option 2: GA includes hard-stop on severe p99 regression as default.
Tradeoff: Option 2 increases risk of false positives and support burden; Option 1 is safer, aligns with ‘safe operations’ messaging.

Decision B: Beta expansion timing (accounts/regions)
• Recommendation: expand to 3 design partners + 2 additional opt-in accounts after (1) propagation lag alert is stable and (2) attribution drop rate < targets for 7 days.

Slide 11 — Asks (what we need to stay on April GA track)
Ask 1: SRE time (2–3 days this sprint)
• Owners: Sean Gallagher + Rafael Mendes
• Needed to: finalize alert thresholds, runbook review, auto-stop kill switch policy, and game day coordination.

Ask 2: Design bandwidth (1 sprint, partial allocation)
• Owners: Tessa Morgan + Kenji Nakamura + Alicia Perez
• Needed to: finalize results dashboard readability (variant comparison, deltas, “insufficient data”), guardrail configuration copy, and audit/change history UI.

Ask 3: Analytics support for freshness semantics
• Owner: Mei Lin (with Logan Wright)
• Needed to: define “data ready” / “last updated” semantics for Console, and document aggregation windows clearly.

Slide 12 — Detailed status by workstream (for reference)
Control plane / experiment service (Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Michael Nguyen)
• Config schema + validation: DONE (including allocation validation, model compatibility checks, max variant constraints).
• State machine: DONE (create → configured → running → stopping/draining → stopped).
• Versioning/migrations: DONE for beta; may need one more migration before GA based on audit export fields.

Policy engine / routing (Jordan Lee, Vikram Singh, Amara Diallo)
• Deterministic bucketing: DONE; stickiness precedence implemented; missing key warning added.
• Precedence with rollouts/fallback: selection applied before fallback; edge case with overlapping rollout policy addressed.

Telemetry & analytics (Logan Wright, Caleb Johnson, Nadia Rahman, Mei Lin)
• Attribution schema: DONE (route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, model_id, region).
• Rollups powering Console: DONE; query cost work ongoing.

Console (Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Felix Schneider, Hannah Rivera)
• Creation wizard + list/detail: DONE behind feature flag.
• Results dashboard: DONE (basic deltas; guardrail status); polish required for clarity + performance at scale.
• Audit view/export: view in progress; export fields in progress.

Security/RBAC (Kaitlyn Nguyen, Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei)
• RBAC gating for mutations: DONE.
• Audit log completeness + export: IN PROGRESS; Helio Financial is pushing on this.

Slide 13 — Next 2 weeks (proposed plan)
Week 1:
• Run game day for propagation lag + attribution drop scenarios (staging) and validate runbooks.
• Land UX polish for results view: data freshness, insufficient data, and guardrail explanations.
• Tighten validation for overlapping experiments on same route (block by default; allow override only with explicit priority + warning).

Week 2:
• Expand beta to additional account(s) in one region first; monitor dashboards for 48 hours.
• Complete audit export fields and finalize enterprise evidence pack draft.

Slide 14 — Appendix: Known open questions
• Overlapping experiments: do we always block on same route, or allow with priority? Current direction: block by default to avoid operator confusion and metrics ambiguity.
• Stickiness default when identifiers missing: current safe default uses a higher-entropy surrogate + warning; do we ever hard-block “no stickiness key”? (recommend warning + allow, but require explicit acknowledgement in UI.)
• Quality metric in Console: which eval score(s) become the default “quality” line item? Applied ML recommends a curated score with normalization + drift guardrail, not raw pass@k.

Slide 15 — Owner contacts

SRE: Sean Gallagher
